hypothesis: The production Stage1 policy often holds a very large cash weight (recently ~77%). Determine whether that cash is (a) the policy's own raw target or (b) a hard-cap artifact, and whether a bounded overlay that recycles part of the idle cash into the unleveraged underlying (SOXX) improves risk-adjusted excess over SOXX on the real production history without giving up drawdown protection.
overlay_definition: Move recycle_fraction of the cash weight into SOXX; the SOXL weight and total risk budget are unchanged.
causality_rule: Targets come from confirmed past slots; returns are qlib open-to-open; no future information enters the overlay.

gates.improvement: best overlay must beat the unmodified policy on Sharpe at the higher cost, and beat SOXX Sharpe

stopping: Exactly the pre-registered recycle family at two costs; no tuning after outcomes. Preserve all results, including failures.
limitations: The real production history is only a handful of sessions; this is diagnostic, not promotion evidence.
The overlay can only reduce cash and raise SOXX exposure; it never raises the SOXL weight.
The frozen production policy parameters are unchanged.
